newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - More bank borrowings.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - More bank borrowings.

text.p: Asian debt markets offered up a couple of new deals Tuesday as well as some chatter on upcoming transactions.

Details emerged on a US$50 million FRCD for Indonesia's Bank Bali. The three-year certificates pay a margin of 78 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate and, with fees, an all-in return of 92.5 basis points.
Arab Banking Corp Singapore, Sanwa International Finance and United Overseas Bank are arrangers.
Bank Bali's FRCD is one of a number of FRCDs for private Indonesian banks that have been launched over the last week.
The state banks also are expected to borrow. So far this year, only Bapindo and Bank Ekspor Impor Indonesia have tapped the capital markets.
Bapindo's FRN was increased to US$150 million from US$125 million, but bankers said they suspect there wasn't much sell-down of the issue.

Bank Negara Indonesia is expected to be the next state bank to borrow, but bankers said an arranger group has not yet been named. The issue is likely to have a 10-year maturity and a put in year seven, which is common for the state banks issues.

Sources said Korean bank issuers, always a mainstay of the Asian debt markets, are approaching their quotas for the year. Cho Hung is one bank that is planning to borrow. It continues to take bids on its next issue. Hanil Bank also is rumoured to be considering an issue.
Kookmin Bank is coming soon with its HK$1.0 billion deal.
Among the Korean quasi-sovereigns, bankers said Societe Generale has won the mandate for a 2 billion French franc deal for Korea Development Bank.
Chase Manhattan Asia is widely tipped to be the winner of Korea Exchange Bank's US$200 million subordinated floating rate note issue.
Malaysian state oil company Petronas will be roadshowing its global bond in Hong Kong Wednesday. Salomon Brothers and CS First Boston are the leads.

In loans, Thailand's Sinn Bualuang has brought a US$100 million transferable loan certificates deal. The five-year deal has annual put options and pays an all-in return of 117.5 basis points over LIBOR to top tier participants.
Sinn Bualuang was founded in 1986 by Bangkok Bank as a holding company to carry out non-bank financial activities of the bank.
